summary: A lying spinal twist that stretches the glutes, outer hip, and lower back while the shoulders rest on the floor.
steps: Lie on your back with your right leg straight and your left knee bent.
Draw the left knee across your body and guide it toward the floor with your right hand.
Rest your left arm out to the side and turn your head to the left.
Let your tailbone settle toward the floor while your chest reaches the other way.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily, then switch sides.
cues: Knee need not touch the floor

summary: A gentle standing mobility drill that circles the knees to warm up the knees, ankles, and lower legs.
steps: Stand with your feet together and knees slightly bent.
Rest your hands on your knees or waist for support.
Circle your knees slowly in one direction, keeping your feet flat.
Reverse direction after several circles, breathing normally.
mistakes: Forcing a large or uncomfortable range
Locking the knees straight between circles

summary: An explosive vertical jump that drives the knees to the chest, building lower-body power and landing control.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, palms down in front of your chest.
Dip quickly into a quarter squat and jump straight up.
Drive your knees up toward your palms at the top of the jump.
Extend your legs before landing and absorb the impact by bending your hips and knees.
Reset your stance before the next jump.
mistakes: Bending the chest down instead of lifting the knees

summary: A supported raise on parallel bars that lifts the knees toward the chest to strengthen the abdominals and hip flexors.
steps: Support yourself between parallel bars on straight arms with your legs hanging.
Press your shoulders down away from your ears.
Exhale and raise your knees until your thighs pass parallel, curling the pelvis up.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower your legs slowly to the start without swinging.
mistakes: Using momentum to swing the legs up

summary: A kneeling stretch with palms down and fingers turned back that lengthens the wrist and forearm flexors.
steps: Kneel on a mat and place your palms flat with fingers pointing back toward your knees.
Keep your elbows straight and your palms pressed into the floor.
Slowly lean back until you feel a stretch in your wrists and forearms.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily.

summary: A half-kneeling stretch that opens the front of the hip and thigh of the back leg.
steps: Kneel on a mat, then step your right foot forward so the knee is bent and the foot is flat.
Extend your left leg behind you with the top of the foot on the floor.
Tuck your pelvis slightly and shift your weight forward until the front of the left hip stretches.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.
mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of moving the hip

summary: A standing glute kickback that lifts one leg behind you to strengthen the glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Stand tall with feet together and hold a sturdy chair or rail for balance.
Brace your core and keep your standing leg straight.
Exhale and lift one leg back behind you, bending the knee slightly as you squeeze the glute.
Lower the leg slowly to the floor as you inhale.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift higher

summary: A lying core drill that draws the knees toward the chest to strengthen the abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back with legs extended and hands at your sides or under your glutes.
Lift your legs slightly off the floor.
Exhale and bend your knees, pulling your thighs toward your chest with shins parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your abs briefly at the top.
Inhale and extend your legs back out with control.
mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor as the legs extend
Using momentum to pull the knees in

summary: A lying stretch that raises one leg toward the ceiling to lengthen the hamstrings.
steps: Lie on your back, bend one knee, and place that foot flat on the floor.
Raise the other leg toward the ceiling, holding behind the thigh or calf.
Straighten the knee as far as is comfortable, sole facing the ceiling.
Gently draw the leg toward you until you feel a stretch.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.
cues: A bent knee is fine if tight

summary: A kneeling backbend that stretches the quadriceps and hip flexors while opening the chest.
steps: Kneel upright with knees hip-width apart and the tops of your feet on the floor.
Reach back and hold your heels with both hands.
Press your hips forward and lift your chest, arching through the upper back.
Let your head go back gently to look at the ceiling.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily, then come up slowly.
mistakes: Sitting back toward the heels instead of pushing the hips forward

summary: A face-down back-extension hold that strengthens the spinal muscles while the abdominals stay braced.
steps: Lie face down with your arms out to the sides.
Brace lightly and lift your chest off the floor using your back muscles.
Keep your arms relaxed and avoid pushing with your hands.
Keep your neck in line with your gaze slightly ahead of you.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then lower slowly.
cues: Lift with the back, not the arms
mistakes: Cranking the neck back to look up

summary: A partner contract-relax stretch in a butterfly position that lengthens the inner thighs.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and the soles of your feet together.
Have your partner place their hands on your knees.
Press your knees together against your partner's resistance for several seconds without moving.
Relax fully as your partner gently eases your knees toward the floor.
Tell your partner when the stretch is enough, and hold it there.
mistakes: Partner pushing too hard or too fast
Holding your breath during the press

summary: A partner contract-relax twist that stretches the outer hip and glutes of the crossed leg.
steps: Lie on your back with legs extended.
Bend one knee and cross it over your body toward the floor.
Have your partner kneel beside you, holding your shoulder down and the crossed knee.
Try to lift the knee for several seconds while your partner prevents movement.
Relax as your partner gently presses the knee toward the floor, then switch sides.
mistakes: Opposite shoulder lifting off the floor

summary: A partner contract-relax stretch with the shin crossed over the body that targets the glutes and outer hip.
steps: Lie on your back with your partner kneeling beside you.
Lift one leg and rotate it so the foot sits over the opposite hip, shin across your body.
Have your partner hold your knee and ankle in place.
Push your leg into your partner's hands for several seconds without moving.
Relax as your partner gently eases the leg toward your chest, then switch sides.
mistakes: Lower back lifting off the floor

summary: A partner contract-relax stretch with one leg raised that lengthens the hamstrings and calf.
steps: Lie on your back with legs extended and your partner kneeling beside you.
Raise one straight leg and let your partner support it at the ankle or on their shoulder.
Press the heel down toward the floor for several seconds as your partner resists.
Relax as your partner gently moves the leg toward your head.
Tell your partner when to stop, then switch sides.
mistakes: Bottom leg lifting off the floor

summary: A partner contract-relax stretch lying face down that lengthens the quadriceps and hip flexors.
steps: Lie face down with your partner kneeling beside you.
Bend one knee, bringing the heel toward your glutes.
Have your partner hold your knee and ankle.
Try to straighten the knee for several seconds while your partner prevents movement.
Relax as your partner gently presses the foot toward your glutes, then switch sides.

summary: A standing torso twist that gently stretches the middle back and obliques.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hands on your hips.
Keep your hips facing forward and your spine tall.
Rotate your upper body to one side until you feel a stretch.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then twist to the other side.

summary: A pull-up with one palm facing you and one facing away that builds back and biceps strength.
steps: Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width, one palm facing you and one facing away.
Hang with straight arms and your shoulders engaged.
Exhale and pull until your chin clears the bar, keeping the underhand elbow close to your body.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly to a full hang, and swap hand positions on your next set.

summary: A crunch with the feet elevated that rotates one elbow toward the opposite knee to work the obliques and abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back with your feet resting on a bench or chair and knees bent.
Place one hand beside your head and rest the other arm on the floor.
Exhale and lift that shoulder, rotating your elbow toward the opposite knee.
Lower slowly with control.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hand

summary: A side-lying crunch that lifts the upper elbow toward the hip to target the obliques.
steps: Lie on your right side with legs stacked and knees slightly bent.
Place your left hand behind your head.
Exhale and crunch your left elbow toward your hip, lifting your shoulder off the floor.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly, then switch sides.
mistakes: Pulling the head with the hand

summary: A side-lying stretch that holds the top foot behind you to lengthen the quadriceps and hip flexors.
steps: Lie on your right side with your right knee bent in front of you for stability.
Bend your left knee and hold your left foot with your left hand.
Press your left hip forward while pushing the foot back into your hand.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A lying stretch with one leg hanging off a bench that lengthens the quadriceps and hip flexor.
steps: Lie on your back on a bench close to one edge.
Let the outside leg and arm hang over the side.
Bend that knee and hold the top of the foot.
Draw your belly in to keep the lower back neutral, then press the foot into your hand.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A standing stretch that leans a bent arm into a wall to lengthen the lats and side of the torso.
steps: Stand beside a wall or doorway.
Place your bent forearm on the wall above shoulder height.
Slowly lean your body toward the wall until you feel a stretch along your side.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A face-down stretch that holds one foot while lifting the chest, opening the quads, hip flexor, and chest.
steps: Lie face down with your left hand tucked under your left hip for padding.
Bend your right knee and hold the foot with your right hand.
Lift the foot toward the ceiling while lifting your shoulders off the floor.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A single-arm dead hang from a bar that builds grip, lat, and shoulder strength for advanced pulling.
steps: Grip the bar with one hand using an overhand grip.
Lift your feet so your full weight hangs from that arm.
Draw your shoulder slightly down so it stays active rather than fully relaxed.
Keep your body still with the free arm by your side.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then switch sides.
mistakes: Hanging passively with the shoulder up by the ear

summary: A lying stretch that pulls one knee to the chest to ease the glutes and lower back.
steps: Lie on your back with both legs extended.
Bend one knee and hold just below it with both hands.
Gently draw that knee toward your chest, keeping the other leg long.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A standing reach with interlaced fingers that lengthens the abdominals, lats, and arms.
steps: Stand tall and interlace your fingers.
Turn your palms up and press your arms overhead.
Keep your shoulders away from your ears and draw your tailbone down.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily.

summary: A partner contract-relax stretch with the elbow bent overhead that lengthens the triceps.
steps: Sit upright on the floor with your partner behind you.
Raise one arm and bend the elbow so your hand reaches down your back.
Have your partner hold your elbow and wrist.
Try to straighten the arm for several seconds while your partner prevents movement.
Relax as your partner gently increases the stretch, then switch sides.
mistakes: Arching the back as the arm moves

summary: A floor drill that tilts the pelvis and peels into a bridge hold, mobilizing the lower back and engaging the glutes.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and heels under your knees.
Draw your belly in and tilt your pelvis to lift only your tailbone.
Keep peeling your spine off the floor into a bridge, leaving your neck and shoulders down.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then roll down one segment at a time.
mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
Lifting the whole spine at once

summary: A seated band stretch that turns the sole inward to lengthen the muscles along the outside of the lower leg.
steps: Sit with one leg extended and loop a belt or band around that foot.
Lift the heel slightly off the floor.
Pull the band so the sole turns inward and the inside of the foot draws toward you.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: An explosive push-up in which your hands leave the floor, building upper-body power in the chest and triceps.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands about shoulder-width apart and body straight.
Lower your chest toward the floor under control.
Push up as hard as you can so your hands leave the floor.
Land with soft elbows and flow straight into the next lowering.
mistakes: Hips sagging or piking during the push
Shortening the range to get airborne

summary: A seated band stretch that turns the sole outward to lengthen the deep calf and inner ankle.
steps: Sit with one leg extended and loop a belt or band around that foot.
Lift the heel slightly off the floor.
Pull the band so the sole turns outward and the outside of the foot draws toward you.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A push-up that rotates into a side plank hold, training the chest, shoulders, and obliques together.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands just outside shoulder width.
Lower into a push-up with your body straight, then press back up.
Shift onto one hand and rotate sideways, reaching the top arm to the ceiling.
Stack or stagger your feet and lift your hips into a straight line.
Hold the side plank, breathing steadily, then return to plank and switch sides.
mistakes: Hips dropping in the side plank
Twisting the hips before the shoulders
Support hand far from under the shoulder

summary: A push-up with hands set wide that shifts more of the work to the chest and front of the shoulders.
steps: Set up in a high plank with hands wider than shoulder width and body straight.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Inhale and bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor.
Exhale and press the floor away to return to straight arms.
mistakes: Hands so wide the range becomes very short

summary: A push-up with hands closer than shoulder width that emphasizes the triceps.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands just inside shoulder width.
Keep your elbows close to your sides.
Inhale and lower until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Exhale and press back up to straight arms.

summary: A push-up with the feet raised on a bench that shifts more load onto the upper chest and shoulders.
steps: Place your toes on a bench or box behind you and your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulders.
Walk your hands so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Inhale and lower until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Exhale and press back to straight arms.
mistakes: Head reaching for the floor before the chest

summary: A push-up practiced with both close and wide hand positions to train the chest, triceps, and shoulders from different angles.
steps: Set up in a high plank with hands wider than shoulder width and body straight.
Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor, then press back up.
Bring your hands closer than shoulder width with elbows tucked.
Lower and press the same way, keeping your body rigid.
Alternate between the two hand positions within the set.
mistakes: Shortening the range on the close grip

summary: A side-lying band stretch that pulls the top heel toward the glutes to lengthen the quadriceps.
steps: Lie on your side and loop a belt or band around your top foot.
Bend the top knee and extend the hip, bringing the heel toward your glutes.
Hold the band over your shoulder or overhead and pull gently to deepen the stretch.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A hands-and-knees drill that extends one leg behind you to work the glutes and thigh while the trunk stays still.
steps: Start on hands and knees with knees under hips and hands under shoulders.
Brace your core and keep your gaze slightly ahead.
Extend one leg back and up, straightening the hip and knee.
Return the knee under the hip with control.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift higher

summary: A squat jump that reaches both arms overhead at full extension to build lower-body power.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms close to your body.
Squat halfway down.
Explode up as high as you can, extending through hips, knees, and ankles and reaching overhead.
Land softly, absorbing the impact by bending your hips and knees.

summary: A standing stick drill that raises straight arms behind the body to mobilize the shoulders and stretch the chest.
steps: Stand tall holding a broomstick or dowel behind your hips with a wide, overhand grip.
Keep your arms straight and your chest up.
Slowly lift the stick up and away from your back as far as is comfortable.
Lower it back with control, never forcing the range.

summary: A low lunge stretch that lengthens the front-leg hamstring and the back-leg hip flexor.
steps: From standing, step one leg back and lower your hands to the floor on either side of your front foot.
Keep the front heel down, sliding the back leg farther back if it lifts.
Gently lift your hips toward the ceiling to bias the hamstring, then lower them again.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A lying core drill that alternates the legs up and down to build abdominal endurance.
steps: Lie on your back with arms by your sides, palms down.
Press your lower back into the floor and lift both legs slightly off the floor.
Raise one leg higher while lowering the other to just above the floor.
Switch legs in a steady scissor rhythm, breathing throughout.
Lower both legs to the floor to finish.
mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor
Heels resting on the floor between kicks

summary: A partner contract-relax stretch with arms extended behind you that lengthens the biceps, chest, and front shoulders.
steps: Sit on the floor with knees bent and your partner standing behind you.
Extend your arms straight back with palms facing each other.
Have your partner hold your wrists.
Try to bend your elbows for several seconds while your partner prevents movement.
Relax as your partner gently lifts your wrists, and say when the stretch is enough.
mistakes: Partner lifting too far or too fast
Rounding forward as the arms rise

summary: A seated stretch that draws the toes toward you to lengthen the calf and back of the leg.
steps: Sit tall with one knee bent and that foot flat on the floor.
Straighten the other leg and flex the ankle.
Pull the toes toward you with a towel, band, or your hand.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A seated core drill on a bench that draws the knees and torso together to strengthen the abdominals.
steps: Sit on the edge of a bench, hold its sides, and lean your torso back at about 45 degrees.
Extend your legs in front of you, slightly below bench height.
Exhale and pull your knees toward your chest as you bring your torso toward them.
Pause briefly.
Inhale and extend back to the start with control.

summary: A seated single-leg stretch that hinges forward over a straight leg to lengthen the hamstring.
steps: Sit with your right leg extended and the sole of your left foot against your right inner thigh.
Sit tall, then hinge forward from your hips.
Reach toward your ankle until you feel a stretch behind the thigh.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A partner contract-relax stretch with arms drawn back that opens the front shoulders and chest.
steps: Sit upright with knees bent and your partner standing behind you.
Extend your arms out to the sides, palms down, and move them back as far as comfortable.
Have your partner hold your wrists.
Press your arms forward for several seconds while your partner prevents movement.
Relax as your partner gently draws your arms farther back, and say when to stop.
mistakes: Partner pulling too far or too fast

summary: A partner contract-relax stretch in a seated figure-four position that lengthens the glutes.
steps: Sit with knees bent and cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Have your partner stand behind you with hands on your shoulders.
Lean forward, then push your torso back against your partner for several seconds without moving.
Relax as your partner gently presses your torso forward.
Tell your partner when the stretch is enough, then switch sides.
mistakes: Rounding the back instead of hinging

summary: A partner contract-relax seated forward fold that lengthens the hamstrings and calves.
steps: Sit with legs extended and your partner standing behind you.
Lean forward and have your partner place their hands on your shoulders.
Push your torso back against your partner for several seconds without moving.
Relax as your partner gently presses you farther forward.
Tell your partner when the stretch is enough.
mistakes: Rounding the back instead of hinging

summary: A seated band stretch that pulls the toes back to lengthen the hamstrings and calf of one leg.
steps: Sit with both legs extended and loop a belt or band around one foot.
Sit tall and lean forward slightly from the hips.
Pull the band to draw the toes back toward you.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A seated tuck on a bench that brings the knees and chest together to build abdominal strength.
steps: Sit on a bench holding its sides, torso leaning back and legs extended slightly below bench height.
Brace your core and keep your shoulders down.
Exhale and tuck your knees toward your chest while curling your torso forward to meet them.
Pause briefly in the tuck.
Inhale and extend your legs and lean back to the start with control.
mistakes: Leaning back too far between tucks

summary: A seated side bend from a butterfly position that stretches the obliques and side of the torso.
steps: Sit tall with the soles of your feet together a short distance in front of your hips.
Place one hand on the floor beside you and the other hand behind your head.
Lift that elbow toward the ceiling as you lean your torso to the opposite side.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A gentle mobility drill that rolls the shoulders through full circles to loosen the shoulders and upper traps.
steps: Stand or sit tall with your arms relaxed at your sides.
Roll your shoulders forward, up, back, and down in a smooth circle.
Reverse direction after several circles.
Move both shoulders together or one at a time.

summary: A standing shrug hold that lifts the shoulders toward the ears to engage the upper traps and shoulders.
steps: Stand tall with your arms relaxed at your sides.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
Lower your shoulders slowly and let them relax.
mistakes: Rolling the shoulders forward as they lift

summary: A cross-body arm stretch that lengthens the back of the shoulder and upper back.
steps: Stand or sit tall.
Bring one straight arm across your chest.
Use the other hand to gently press the arm toward your chest, just above the elbow.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A side-lying crunch that lifts the legs and upper body together to strengthen the obliques.
steps: Lie on one side with legs stacked and straight, bottom forearm on the floor for support.
Place your top hand lightly behind your head.
Exhale and lift both legs while crunching your upper body toward them.
Pause briefly with your obliques squeezed.
Lower your legs and torso slowly, then switch sides.
mistakes: Rolling onto the back instead of staying on your side
Pulling on the head with the hand

summary: A standing side leg swing that moves one leg out and back across the body to work the outer and inner hip.
steps: Stand beside a chair or wall and hold it for support.
Balance on the inside leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Keeping the outside leg straight, raise it out to the side.
Let it swing back down and across in front of the standing leg.
Gradually increase the range, then switch sides.
mistakes: Leaning the torso away from the lifting leg

summary: A side-lying stretch that draws the top leg up and open to lengthen the inner thigh and hamstring.
steps: Lie on your right side with your right knee bent in front of you and your head on your hand.
Lift your left leg and hold it behind the knee, or at the foot for more stretch.
Pull the knee toward your left shoulder while letting the leg open toward the floor.
Straighten the leg to deepen the stretch if comfortable.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A gentle seated or standing stretch that tilts the head to lengthen the side of the neck.
steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Tilt your head slowly toward one shoulder.
Rest the same-side hand on your head for a light assist if needed.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A lateral broad jump that builds side-to-side power and landing control in the legs.
steps: Stand in an athletic stance with feet hip-width apart, chest up, knees slightly bent.
Load your hips and lean toward the direction you will jump.
Swing your arms and drive through hips, knees, and ankles to jump sideways as far as you can.
Land facing forward with feet hip-width apart, absorbing the impact through your legs.
Reset and jump back the other way.
mistakes: Twisting the body in the air

summary: A wide-grip pull-up that shifts toward one hand and then the other, loading each arm more heavily in turn.
steps: Grip the bar wide with palms facing forward and hang with straight arms.
Lean back slightly, lift your chest, and set your shoulders down.
Pull up toward your left hand until the bar nears your upper chest.
Lower under control to a full hang.
Pull toward your right hand next, alternating sides.
mistakes: Swinging or kipping into the lean

summary: A standing stretch that pulls one arm across the body to lengthen the upper back, lats, and rear shoulder.
steps: Stand tall and cross your left arm in front of your body.
Hold your left wrist with your right hand at hip level, left elbow bent.
Slowly straighten the left arm and pull it up toward shoulder height.
Feel the stretch in your upper back rather than the shoulder joint.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A side-lying overhead reach that lengthens the lats and the full side of the body.
steps: Lie on your left side with your left knee bent in front of you for stability.
Straighten your right leg and rest that foot on the floor behind your left leg.
Reach your right arm overhead and hold that wrist with your left hand, gently drawing it long.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A single-leg hop that kicks the heel toward the glutes to train leg power and coordination.
steps: Stand on one leg with the other knee raised in front of you.
Dip slightly and jump up off the standing leg, extending hip, knee, and ankle.
In the air, bend the jumping knee to bring that heel toward your glutes.
Bring the leg back under your hips and land softly.
Keep the raised knee steady throughout, then switch sides.
mistakes: Leaning forward to reach the heel

summary: A one-leg bridge that strengthens the glutes and hamstrings while challenging hip stability.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Lift one foot and draw that knee toward your chest.
Drive through the heel of the planted foot to lift your hips.
Pause at the top with your hips level.
Lower slowly to the floor, then switch sides.
mistakes: Hips tilting or rotating toward the free leg
Arching the lower back at the top

summary: A side-to-side hop on one leg that builds ankle stiffness, balance, and lateral power.
steps: Stand on one leg beside a line or small cone, knee slightly bent.
Hop sideways over the line, landing on the same leg.
Absorb the landing, then rebound straight back to the start.
Keep hopping back and forth, then switch legs.

summary: A partial-range bodyweight squat that builds quad strength and teaches sitting back with the hips.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your hips and knees, sitting the hips back.
Lower until you are partway down, staying above parallel.
Reverse and stand back up to full extension.

summary: A full trunk curl from lying to sitting that strengthens the abdominals and hip flexors.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet anchored under something stable or held by a partner.
Place your hands behind your head or across your chest.
Exhale and curl your upper body up until your torso and thighs form a V.
Pause briefly.
Inhale and lower back down with control.
mistakes: Pulling on the head with the hands

summary: A side-to-side skater bound that mimics skating strides to build leg power, balance, and conditioning.
steps: Stand on your right leg with a slight knee bend, left foot lifted behind you.
Push off sideways to the left, swinging your arms across your body.
Land softly on your left leg, letting the right leg sweep behind you.
Push back to the right and keep alternating in a steady rhythm.

summary: A plank-based drill that brings each knee toward the same-side elbow, working the core, chest, and shoulders.
steps: Start in a plank on your hands and toes with feet together and body straight.
Lift one foot and bring that knee out to the side toward the same elbow.
Return the leg to the start with control.
Repeat on the other side, keeping the hips low and steady.

summary: A seated twist and forward reach that mobilizes the middle and upper back.
steps: Sit tall on a chair with your feet flat on the floor.
Interlace your fingers behind your head, elbows wide and chin slightly tucked.
Rotate your upper body to one side as far as is comfortable.
Lean forward and twist to bring one elbow toward the floor inside the opposite knee.
Hold 20–30 seconds, return upright, then switch sides.

summary: A staggered-stance squat that lowers the back knee toward the floor to strengthen the quads, glutes, and hamstrings.
steps: Stand in a long staggered stance, one foot forward and the back heel lifted.
Keep your torso upright and your weight centered between your feet.
Lower straight down until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Drive through the front foot to rise back up.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Stance too short, front heel lifting

summary: A standing stretch with hands clasped behind the back that lengthens the biceps, chest, and front shoulders.
steps: Stand tall and clasp your hands behind your back.
Straighten your arms and turn your palms to face down.
Lift your arms gently away from your back until you feel a stretch.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily.

summary: A standing stretch with the rear foot raised on a bench that lengthens the quadriceps and hip flexor.
steps: Stand with your back a short stride from a bench or step.
Lift one leg back and rest the instep or ball of the foot on the bench.
Keep the standing knee slightly bent and stand tall.
Tuck your pelvis slightly until you feel a stretch in the front of the thigh.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A standing stretch with the heel on a step that lengthens the calf and the back of the leg.
steps: Place one heel on a low step with that knee straight.
Bend the standing knee slightly, keep your back straight, and rest your other hand on your thigh.
Lean forward and pull the toes of the raised foot toward your knee.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A standing band stretch that hinges over a straight front leg to lengthen the hamstrings and calf.
steps: Loop a belt or band around one foot and step that foot forward.
Bend the back knee and keep the front leg straight.
Lift the front toes and hinge forward from the hips.
Pull the band to draw the top of the foot back.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A standing split-stance stretch that presses the back hip forward to lengthen the hip flexors.
steps: Stand tall with one foot slightly in front of the other.
Bend both knees and lift the back heel.
Tuck your pelvis and press the back hip forward.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A standing side bend that lengthens the obliques and the side of the torso.
steps: Stand with feet slightly wider than hips and knees soft.
Place your right hand on your right hip.
Raise your left arm and rest that hand behind your head.
Lean your torso to the right, keeping your weight even on both feet.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A two-footed forward broad jump that builds horizontal power through the hips, knees, and ankles.
steps: Stand in a partial squat with feet shoulder-width apart.
Swing your arms back as you dip your hips and knees.
Swing your arms forward and jump out as far as you can.
Reach your feet forward and land softly, absorbing the impact through your legs.
Stand up and reset before the next jump.

summary: A standing mobility hold that tilts the pelvis under to ease the lower back and engage the glutes.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Rock your pelvis gently forward and back a few times to find the motion.
Tuck your tailbone forward and under, flattening the lower back.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A bent-knee standing calf stretch that targets the soleus and the Achilles area.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, one foot slightly behind the other.
Bend both knees, keeping the back heel on the floor.
Sink until you feel a stretch low in the back calf.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A standing forward fold that lets the upper body hang to stretch the hamstrings and calves.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart.
Hinge at the hips and fold forward with legs straight but not locked.
Let your head, arms, and hands hang toward the floor.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then roll up slowly.

summary: An overhead towel extension against a partner's resistance that strengthens the triceps.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding one end of a towel overhead with both hands.
Have your partner stand behind you and hold the other end to add resistance.
Keeping your upper arms by your head, lower your hands behind your head by bending the elbows.
Extend your elbows to press the towel back overhead against the resistance.

summary: A breath-driven hold that draws the navel toward the spine to train the deep abdominal muscles.
steps: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and hands on your hips.
Inhale, then exhale fully through your mouth.
Draw your navel in toward your spine and up under your ribs as far as you can.
Hold the contraction, taking small, shallow breaths if needed.
Inhale slowly and relax your abdomen to finish.
mistakes: Lifting the chest instead of drawing in the belly

summary: A suspension-strap rollout that reaches the arms overhead while the trunk resists arching, strengthening the abdominals.
steps: Set suspension straps or rings below waist height and hold the handles.
Lean forward into an incline push-up position with straight arms.
Keeping your arms straight, let your shoulders open as your hands travel overhead and your body lowers.
Pause at the farthest point you can control with a neutral spine.
Pull your arms back down to return to the start.
mistakes: Lower back sagging at the end range

summary: A push-up on suspension straps or rings that demands extra shoulder stability while training the chest and triceps.
steps: Anchor suspension straps or rings securely and hold a handle in each hand.
Walk your feet back into a plank with straight arms and a rigid body.
Lower slowly until your elbows pass 90 degrees.
Pause, then press back up to straight arms.

summary: A plank with the feet in suspension straps that draws the knees to the chest to strengthen the abdominals.
steps: Set the handles a short distance off the floor and place your feet in them.
Walk your hands into a push-up plank facing away from the anchor.
Draw your knees toward your chest, letting your pelvis tilt and spine curl.
Extend your legs back to the plank with control.

summary: A bodyweight row on suspension straps that strengthens the middle back, lats, and biceps.
steps: Set straps or rings at about chest height and hold a handle in each hand.
Lean back with straight arms and a rigid body, chest up.
Pull your chest toward the handles, drawing your shoulder blades back.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly to straight arms.

summary: A split squat with the rear foot in a suspension strap that strengthens the front-leg quads and glutes and challenges balance.
steps: Set the handles low, around knee height, and face away from the anchor.
Place your rear foot in the handle behind you and stand tall on the front leg.
Lower by bending the front knee and hip until the front thigh nears parallel.
Drive through the front heel to return to standing.
Switch sides.

summary: A seated wide-leg forward fold that stretches the hamstrings and inner thighs.
steps: Sit tall with your legs extended wide in a V.
Place your hands on the floor in front of you.
Hinge forward from the hips as far as is comfortable.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily.

summary: A lying crunch with the legs raised that reaches the hands toward the toes to strengthen the abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back and raise your legs nearly vertical with a slight knee bend.
Reach your arms up toward your feet.
Exhale and curl your shoulders off the floor, reaching your hands toward your toes.
Lower your shoulders slowly to the floor.
mistakes: Legs drifting down as you crunch

summary: A stretch that brings one arm across the body and over the opposite shoulder to lengthen the triceps.
steps: Stand or sit tall.
Bring your right arm across your body, reaching over your left shoulder.
Hold the right elbow with your left hand and gently press it back.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: An overhead stretch that pulls the bent elbow behind the head to lengthen the triceps and lats.
steps: Stand or sit tall and reach one hand down behind your head, elbow pointing up.
Hold that elbow with your other hand.
Gently pull the elbow toward the center until you feel a stretch.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A crunch with the legs held up in a tuck that strengthens the abdominals while the lower back stays down.
steps: Lie on your back, cross your ankles, and lift your legs so the thighs are vertical and knees bent.
Cross your arms over your chest.
Exhale and curl your shoulders off the floor toward your knees.
Pause briefly, then lower slowly with control.

summary: A forward reach with clasped hands that rounds the upper back to stretch between the shoulder blades.
steps: Stand or sit tall and interlace your fingers in front of you, thumbs pointing down.
Reach your hands forward at shoulder height.
Round your upper back and let your shoulder blades spread apart.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily.

summary: A seated forward fold hugging the thighs that stretches the hamstrings and the middle and lower back.
steps: Sit with your legs extended and knees together.
Bend forward and hug your thighs from underneath.
Bring your chest down toward your knees.
Gently pull your back away from your knees to stretch the middle back.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily.

summary: A standing overhead reach with palms together that stretches the shoulders, chest, and lats.
steps: Stand tall and extend both arms overhead, palms touching.
Keep your back straight and ribs down.
Slowly press your hands up and slightly back.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily.

summary: A hanging drill that alternates quick knee drives to build abdominal and hip flexor endurance.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms and legs straight.
Brace your core to keep your body still.
Drive one knee up as high as you can.
Lower it as you drive the other knee up, alternating quickly.
Keep alternating without swinging, then lower both legs to finish.
mistakes: Swinging the body to drive the knees

summary: A lying cross-body leg reach that stretches the outer hip, glutes, and lower back.
steps: Lie on your back with arms out to the sides and legs straight.
Lift one straight leg and cross it over your body toward the opposite hand.
Keep both shoulders on the floor as the leg lowers toward the ground.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then return and switch sides.
mistakes: Flinging the leg across with momentum

summary: A single-leg squat to a box that builds unilateral leg strength and control on the way to a pistol squat.
steps: Stand on one leg a short step in front of a sturdy box or chair.
Extend the other leg straight out in front of you.
Sit back and down slowly until you lightly touch the box.
Pause briefly without relaxing.
Drive through the working foot to stand, keeping the free leg off the floor.
Switch sides.

summary: A half-kneeling rotation that opens the upper back to improve thoracic spine mobility.
steps: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat in front of you, hips square.
Extend both arms straight in front of you at shoulder height, palms together.
Exhale and rotate one arm open and back, turning your chest and eyes with it.
Inhale and return to the start.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Rotating the hips instead of the upper back
Arching the lower back to reach farther

summary: A kneeling rollout with an ab wheel that challenges the abdominals to resist arching the lower back.
steps: Kneel on a mat holding the ab wheel handles below your shoulders.
Brace your core and tuck your pelvis slightly.
Roll the wheel forward slowly, lengthening your body as far as you can control.
Pull the wheel back toward your knees using your abs.
mistakes: Lower back sagging at the far end
Hips shooting back first on the return
Rolling farther than you can control

summary: A short-range floor curl that lifts the shoulders and upper back to strengthen the abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Place your hands lightly behind your head or across your chest.
Exhale and curl your shoulders and upper back off the floor.
Keep your lower back on the floor and pause briefly.
Lower slowly with control.
